items: DO: Email within a few days

captions.facebook:
Recruiting Reality Check: your son went to the camp. Now what?

A lot of families treat the camp as the finish line. It's really the start. Coaches can see dozens of players in a single day, and a short, specific follow-up email is one of the simplest ways to help them remember yours.

What works:
✅ Send it within a few days, while the camp is still fresh.
✅ Mention one specific moment: a drill, a piece of feedback, a conversation with a coach.
✅ Keep it short: a thank-you, that moment, his grad year and position, and his video link.

What doesn't:
❌ The same copy-and-paste message to every school.
❌ A parent writing it. Coaches want to hear from the player himself.

Parents who've been through it: did a follow-up email ever lead to a real conversation with a coach? And if you have a recruiting question, leave it below. We may answer it in a future Reality Check.

The offseason is when a lot of recruiting work quietly gets done. Here's a simple winter game plan before spring arrives:

1. Retest his key numbers. Exit velo, 60 time, velocity or pop time. Coaches care about where he is now, not where he was last summer.
2. Update his skills video with his best current clips.
3. Refresh his target list. If his numbers moved, the levels that fit him best may have moved too.
4. Email coaches his spring schedule. Dates and locations make it easy for a coach to come see him play.

None of these guarantee interest from a program. They make sure the coaches he's contacting see the most current, most accurate version of him.

Which of these is your family tackling first this winter? Or what would you add to the list?
